items.headline: Lead: The board still hasn't flipped — Sunday still goes through Check
paragraphs: I checked the app again after the evening refresh. It is still the November 2 board. Same snapshot, Week 8 games, twelve days old. It still lists Sam Darnold as Seattle's starter and Kyler Murray as Minnesota's starter, and it knows nothing about Sunday.

items.takeaway: The board is still the November 2 board, so nothing on it applies to Sunday — run your number through Check, and watch inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: Injuries: Saturday's changes — Walker is out, Watson is back
paragraphs: The one downgrade since this morning: Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III went from questionable to out with a groin injury. He will not play at Atlanta. That is the only name that moved the wrong way today.

Going the other way: Deshaun Watson is back under center for Cleveland on Sunday after missing last week in concussion protocol. Kirk Cousins starts for Minnesota with Kyler Murray out. Garrett Wilson is trending to play against Buffalo — he practiced fully Friday even with the questionable tag, and so did Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell.

Two more from Saturday: Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth was added to the injury report with an illness and is questionable for Sunday night. The Patriots activated fullback Reggie Gilliam and guard Greg Van Roten from injured reserve, and both are still questionable for Munich.
Still questionable from this morning: A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson in Munich, Amon-Ra St. Brown in Munich too, and Trent Williams in Dallas. Inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff.
items.takeaway: Walker is out, Watson and Cousins start, Wilson is trending to play — and the Munich questionable names are still decided at inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: Weather: final check — nothing flagged, same as this morning
paragraphs: No wind flag anywhere on Sunday. Every outdoor game stays under the 15 mph sustained wind line.

Cleveland is still the wettest open-air spot — a light rain chance and a north wind around 12 mph with gusts in the teens. MetLife has the strongest gusts, around 20 mph, with almost no rain chance. Munich is calm and overcast in the 40s. Dallas plays under a closed roof, so the rain outside never reaches the field.
Weather is a fact to know, not a reason to bet a total. The number you care about is still the one your book is offering — run it through Check.
items.takeaway: No wind flag anywhere on Sunday — Cleveland has the only rain chance and MetLife the strongest gusts, and neither reaches the line that usually matters.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — Sunday still goes through Check
paragraphs: The board refreshes every morning and evening, but I checked twice tonight and it is still showing the November 2 snapshot. It is twelve days old, it is still showing Week 8, and it still lists Darnold as Seattle's starter and Murray as Minnesota's starter — both wrong for Sunday.

That does not leave you without the app. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. It is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
If your book's number is different from the one on the board — and right now every book's number is different, because the board is twelve days old — Check is how you use the app today.
items.takeaway: The board is twelve days old and still showing Week 8, so Sunday's prices go through Check — type in your book's line and the app gives a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.

items.headline: A questionable starter is a moving number
paragraphs: The app's numbers are built on the expected starter. When the starter changes, the number changes with it — and the old verdict is dead.

That is what the inactives list does. A.J. Brown, Stevenson and Amon-Ra St. Brown are all questionable for Munich, and inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff. If one of them sits, the line moves, and the price you liked an hour ago is a different bet.
So run the number again after the news lands. Tap Check, type in the new line and price, and let the app give you a fresh verdict on the team that is actually playing.
items.takeaway: The app prices the expected starter — when inactives change the starter, the old verdict is dead, so Check the new number.

items.headline: Learn the Game: key numbers — the 3 and the 7
paragraphs: In football, most games are decided by 3 points or 7 points — a field goal, or a touchdown with the extra point. Those are the key numbers, and books price around them.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say a favorite is -3. If you take that number, you win only if they win by more than 3 — win by exactly 3 and it is a push, your money back. If the line moves to -2.5, that same win by 3 now pays you. The half-point across the key number is worth real money, which is why it is called the hook.
That is why a move across 3 or 7 matters more than a move from, say, -6 to -6.5. Before you take any price, run it through Check and see what the app says about it.
items.takeaway: Key numbers are 3 and 7 — a line crossing one of them changes your bet more than a move anywhere else, so watch for the hook.

items.headline: Small moves today, and the big numbers held
paragraphs: The Jaguars are still -10.5, and the 49ers-Cowboys total is still 55.5. I saw no reported move on the Lions in Munich in today's checks.

What did move: the 49ers ticked toward Dallas, from -4.5 down to -3.5 at DraftKings, while the total held at 55.5. The Munich total slipped a point, from 50.5 to 49.5. The Jaguars total went the other way, up to 46.5.

The board itself is unchanged — still the November 2 snapshot — so there is no new app number to compare against. Any move that happens tonight will show up on your book first, and Check is how you test it.
On the splits: the free VSiN page tonight showed a college basketball row and no NFL row, so there is no fresh public-versus-money read. That is not a Fade — it is just no data to read.
items.takeaway: 49ers -4.5 to -3.5, Munich total down a point, Jaguars total up to 46.5 — the big numbers held, and the free splits page had no NFL row to read tonight.

items.headline: Tonight's job: set your Sunday board before bed
paragraphs: Saturday night is prep. Know which questionable names your bets depend on: A.J. Brown, Stevenson and Amon-Ra St. Brown in Munich, Wilson against Buffalo, Williams in Dallas. Munich inactives land about 8:00 a.m. ET.

Wait only for inactives if your bet needs a questionable player. Otherwise, if your book has a good number right now and Check says bet, bet it now. Waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too, and the Sunday late rush on big-name teams can push a line past the app's playable number.
Set an alarm if Munich is on your card — 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff, inactives about 8:00 a.m. ET. The early game waits for no one.
items.takeaway: Know your questionable names tonight — wait only for inactives if your bet needs one, otherwise bet a good number now if Check says bet. Munich kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET.
